Resolves #20452

A Store now lets go of the Model it created. It releases that Model on destroy and on replacement, and it never touches a passed instance. `Model#release()` drops the instance-registry entry and the cached record class without destroying the Model. Records outlive their Store and read their schema through that Model, so it is collected with the last record that still reads it. `Model#destroy()` now drops its record class as well. A release or destroy removes only its own entries: an id that a successor reused stays the successor's.

Evidence: L2 (unit tests on the single-thread engine setup) → L2 required (every AC is a data-layer lifecycle observable; no rendered or host effect).

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `Store.spec.mjs` › Neo.data.Store Model ownership › "destroy() releases a Model the Store created from a class" and "… from a config" (registry entry and record class gone; a retained record still reads and writes) |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: › "replacing a Model the Store created releases it; its records keep working" |
| AC-3 | CI-covered: › "a passed Model instance stays its owner's, on destroy and on replacement" |
| AC-4 | CI-covered: same test, last arm (the record class is present, then gone after `shared.destroy()`) |
| AC-5 | CI-covered: `ComboBoxSharedStore.spec.mjs` (private view Models retired, source Model alive) and `Chip.spec.mjs` › "replaces its owned Store only after the shared chip projection detaches" |
| AC-6 | Outside-CI: the four original ownership specs on base `03f88c6992` source fail 4/4 and pass at head; the id-reuse arm fails on this PR's first head source ("a late release") and passes at head |
| AC-7 | `learn/guides/datahandling/UsingStores.md`: the teardown no longer destroys `store.model`; destroying the Store is enough |

## Deltas from ticket

- My first cut destroyed the created Model, as the ticket originally prescribed. The unit census caught `Chip.spec.mjs` failing, because `record.get()` on a retained record reads the destroyed Model. So the shape became release, not destroy. #20452's body records that derivation.
- Sophie found that a released Model is unregistered but alive, so its id can be reused. A late `release()` or a first `destroy()` of the old Model then removed the successor's registration and record class. The fix sits in the layers that own those entries. `manager.Base#unregister()` removes a passed reference only while it still holds its key's registration; a key still removes its entry, and every caller passes a key or its registered object. Before the instance manager exists, `core.Base#destroy()`'s `Neo.idMap` fallback deletes only its own entry; Sophie's bootstrap probe found that path. `RecordFactory` remembers the class it built per Model and releases only that one. Arm: "a released Model whose id a successor reused retires nothing of the successor's", run once per registry (instance manager and bootstrap id map).
- #20449 merged first, so AC-7 became live and is delivered here. The same guide's picker paragraph was #20453's merge-order AC. #20458 merged before that edit could ride along, so this PR rewrites it too, in the same file: an open picker now repaints an edited label, and an edit does not re-run the picker's query.
- `dev` is merged in twice (no rebase of the pushed branch).

## Test Evidence

- Red-first on base source versus head with the same command: base 4 failed, head 4 passed. The id-reuse arm fails on this PR's first head source and passes at head.

### `@neo-gpt-sophie` commented on 2026-11-06T14:21:37Z

### RA-1 disposition preparation: early-registry destroy still open

This is the existing action from [review 5801138395](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/20457#pullrequestreview-5801138395), not a new demand round:

> Make cleanup through an old Model act only on that Model's own instance-registry and record-class entries. After automatic release and explicit ID reuse, both a late `oldModel.release()` and its first `oldModel.destroy()` must leave the replacement Model registered and its cached constructor unchanged.

At exact `6c9b2846c79efd36f9f4f0bb8c1e86fde343514e`, I repeated that sequence in a fresh Node process **without importing InstanceManager**, and asserted `Base.instanceManagerAvailable === false` before creating the fixtures. This exercises the actual `Neo.idMap` bootstrap path rather than changing a loaded manager's flags.

| Old-handle action | Successor at `Neo.idMap[id]` before → after | Cached successor constructor unchanged |
|---|---|---|
| `release()` | true → true | true |
| first `destroy()` | true → **false** | true |

The release and cache guards work. The remaining path is `Model.destroy()` → `Base.destroy()`, whose early-registry branch still unconditionally deletes `Neo.idMap[me.id]`. The existing new spec imports InstanceManager, so it cannot witness that branch.

**RA-1 remains open only at this original root-identity edge:** explicit destruction of the old Model must preserve the successor's early-registry entry while retiring the old object. Keep the manager-backed and retained-record controls alongside this bootstrap control. Current CI is still pending; no formal Round-2 verdict is posted here.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge:** A released Model remains alive, while its registration slot can be reused. At exact head `e2e5061f72342c281f838d47b9e2d201be739b38`, I ran a Node probe using the real unit setup and unmodified Store/Model/RecordFactory/Instance implementations:

1. Create a Store with a Model config carrying an explicit ID and materialize a record.
2. Keep the old Model; destroy the Store. Confirm the old registration is gone and the retained record still reads.
3. Create a new Model of the same class with that ID, then a Store using it and a record. Confirm the new registration and record-class cache exist.
4. Call the old Model's `release()`. In a separate fresh case, call its first `destroy()` instead.

| Old-handle action | New Model registered before → after | New record class cached before → after | New Model destroyed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `release()` | true → false | true → false | false |
| `destroy()` | true → false | true → false | false |

The relevant paths are `src/data/Model.mjs:124–126` and `:153–161`, plus `src/data/RecordFactory.mjs:391–394`. Cache deletion is by class-name/ID; `Manager#unregister` delegates to a key-based collection removal. The new registration is therefore removed without retiring the new Model itself. Both paths need the same ownership boundary; making only repeated `release()` a no-op leaves the first late `destroy()` destructive.

For reproduction inside the existing Store unit setup, run each action with a fresh ID:

```js
const fields = [{name: 'id', type: 'Integer'}, {name: 'name', type: 'String'}],
      id = 'model-reuse-' + action,
      store = Neo.create(Store, {model: {module: Model, id, fields}, data: [{id: 1, name: 'old'}]}),
      oldModel = store.model;
store.destroy();
const newer = Neo.create(Model, {id, fields}),
      replacement = Neo.create(Store, {model: newer, data: [{id: 2, name: 'new'}]});
oldModel[action](); // action = 'release' or 'destroy'
expect(Neo.get(id)).toBe(newer); // fails: null
```
